clue.text: Fish that is good in its proper place

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is set inside the other here

parts.note: a fish's natural home is the sea
pi, short for pious, is the crossword stock for good

explanation.surface: A fish described as doing well when it is where it belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' looks like I.E. but is only a link; a fish's proper place is taken to be the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is the cuttlefish, loosely counted as a fish in crosswords.

clue.text: Divided about an enclosure, became more biting

indicators.note: about means the dividing word surrounds the enclosure

parts.note: shared means divided up
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Split around a pen, something grew sharper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpened means made keener-edged or more cutting.

clue.text: Smooth tree?

explanation.definitionFit: To plane wood is to make it smooth; the plane is also a broadleaf street tree.

clue.text: A rebel state in the university

parts.note: Jack Cade led a revolt against Henry VI in 1450
ME is the abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: An insurgent region within a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; Jack CADE, a medieval English rebel, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic world, the community of universities.

clue.text: Phrase "I do" can be put in pithy terms

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of phrase and I do may be made into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A remark that a wedding vow can be turned into a pithy saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' signals that PHRASE and IDO are rearranged together into the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To aphorise is to express something as a short memorable maxim.

clue.text: The man to compose a song of praise

indicators.note: to compose here is to arrange the letters of the man in a new order

explanation.surface: A man sets out to write a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a solemn hymn or song of celebration.

clue.text: Difficult business about foundations for road

parts.note: hard means difficult
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A tough firm deals with groundwork for a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal but gives RE. In Britain HARDCORE is broken rubble laid as a road base.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardcore is the compacted rubble used as a base layer under roads.

clue.text: Sappers seize unit position in counterstroke

indicators.note: seize means the sappers' letters grip the others between them

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are the army's sappers
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit
a post is a position

explanation.surface: Army engineers capture a unit's post during a counter-attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick return thrust in fencing, hence a retort.

clue.text: Endorser of a lie about poor Gina

indicators.note: about means the fib's word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a story is a fib or lie

indicators.note: poor suggests the name Gina is in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A signer backs a falsehood concerning unfortunate Gina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges Gina's letters, and 'about' wraps the word for a fib around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A signatory signs a document, thereby endorsing it.

clue.text: Fish about — name of Morris?

indicators.note: about means the fish's letters go around the other

parts.note: the dace is a small river fish

explanation.surface: A fish swims around someone called Morris.
explanation.walkthrough: Morris is not a man here: the morris is a traditional English folk dance with bells and sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: The morris is an example of a folk step routine, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Gypsum, white as a flower after a party

indicators.note: after places the flower's letters behind those of a party

parts.note: Lab is the short form of the Labour Party
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A mineral likened to a pale bloom following a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a party' reads as a celebration but is A plus LAB (Labour); 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine white variety of gypsum used for carving.

clue.text: Father to scold returning godless type

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: returning means the word for scolding is read backwards

parts.note: to nag is to scold persistently

explanation.surface: A dad tells someone off on their return from abandoning faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen with no belief in the Christian God is called this.

clue.text: Liking to participate, showing interest in business

parts.note: a liking is a preference
to share is to take part

explanation.surface: Someone keen to join in shows enthusiasm for commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference share is a stake in a company paying a fixed dividend before ordinary shares.

clue.text: Pistol is back to fetch a lump of gold

indicators.note: is back means the word for pistol is read backwards

parts.note: a pistol is a gun
to fetch is to go and get

explanation.surface: A gunman returns to collect a piece of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a natural lump of precious metal found in the ground.

clue.text: Poet in profit — 'e gets a raincoat

indicators.note: in means the poet is placed inside the profit word

parts.note: gain means profit
a bard is a poet
'e is a dropped-aitch he, giving the letter E

explanation.surface: A poet making money gets himself a coat for wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabardine is a tightly woven cloth, and a mackintosh made from it.

clue.text: Loose living — there's nothing to pay — nothing

parts.note: something free costs nothing
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Dissolute life costs nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Free love is sexual relations without marriage or commitment, a promiscuous lifestyle.

clue.text: Spend more cooking for the seedy feeder

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters of spend more are being worked over into a new shape

explanation.surface: Advice to splash out on food for someone shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seedy' suggests shabby, but means belonging to a seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Endosperm is the tissue inside a seed that nourishes the developing embryo.

clue.text: Shoots the sailor — or Mickey Mouse?

parts.note: to shoot a scene is to film it
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone guns down a seaman, or perhaps a cartoon rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' reads as gunfire but means films; 'the' is a link. Mickey Mouse is an example of a screen celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey Mouse is a famous cinema celebrity, an example of the type.

clue.text: Cheerful young lady on parade

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young upper-class woman
taken as written
to parade one's views is to air them

explanation.surface: A breezy young woman taking part in a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave and carefree, light-heartedly confident.

clue.text: Name applied to lots of blockheads

parts.note: oodles means lots

explanation.surface: A label stuck on plenty of dimwits.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is slang for a fool, so noodles are dunces.

clue.text: Stupid fellow holds the old to be wearied by excess

indicators.note: holds means the oaf's word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a clod is a dull oaf
ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: A dim man clutching an old item finds he has had too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints the count as (8), but the clue builds a six-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cloyed is to be sickened by too much of something sweet or pleasant.

clue.text: Student providing ring by stealing

parts.note: L is a learner, a student driver
if means providing that
ting is the ringing sound of a bell

explanation.surface: A student offers a ring by way of theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting is slang for shoplifting or pilfering.

clue.text: Woman's name on fire grate

parts.note: a fire that is in is still burning
a grid is a grating

explanation.surface: A girl's name appears on a hearth's metal frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire grate' reads as one thing but splits in two; a fire that is 'in' is still alight, as in 'keep the fire in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a girl's given name of Scandinavian origin.

clue.text: Playing false, perhaps, with circus group

parts.note: playing on stage is performing

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word false might be another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Acting deceitfully alongside a troupe from the big top.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea circus was a sideshow claiming trained insects did tricks.

clue.text: After being around I assume it's true

indicators.note: being around means the after word encloses the single letter

parts.note: post is Latin for after

explanation.surface: Once things are around, I suppose it's correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a fact for argument.

clue.text: Some prelates, proud once

indicators.note: some means only part of the word prelates is taken

explanation.surface: Certain bishops were once haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Elate is an archaic adjective meaning exultant or puffed up.

clue.text: Calm, all the same

explanation.surface: Peaceful, but nevertheless so.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means motionless and quiet, and also nevertheless or even so.

clue.text: Call it Ena's loose end

parts.note: to term something is to name or call it

indicators.note: loose means the letters of it and Ena are set free and rearranged

parts.note: the name Ena; the 's is read as is, a link

explanation.surface: A woman named Ena is told to call off something unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to bring to a close or finish.

clue.text: Walk about, certain to be idolised

indicators.note: about means the walking word goes around the other

parts.note: to tread is to walk
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Strolling around, someone is sure of being worshipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cherished and held dear is idolised.

clue.text: Slight trace of a transient light

explanation.surface: A faint sign of a passing glow.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a faint sign, as of hope, and a brief flash of brightness.
